formal_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) (Q : Fin m → Fin m → ℕ → Fin (m + 2 * k * (m * m)) → Prop), 1 ≤ k → (∀ (u v : Fin m) (p : ℕ) (x : Fin (m + 2 * k * (m * m))), Q u v p x ↔ (p = 0 ∧ x.val = u.val) ∨ (p = 2 * k + 1 ∧ x.val = v.val) ∨ (1 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * k ∧ x.val + 1 = m + 2 * k * (u.val * m + v.val) + p)) → ∃ S : SimpleGraph (Fin (m + 2 * k * (m * m))), (∀ x y : Fin (m + 2 * k * (m * m)), S.Adj x y ↔ ∃ u v : Fin m, u < v ∧ H.Adj u v ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p ≤ 2 * k ∧ ((Q u v p x ∧ Q u v (p + 1) y) ∨ (Q u v p y ∧ Q u v (p + 1) x)))
plain_statement: Let H be a graph on Fin m and k >= 1. For an edge u < v of H, position 0 of its path is u, position 2k + 1 is v, and position p, 1 <= p <= 2k, is the vertex of index m + 2k(u m + v) + p - 1 of Fin (m + 2k m^2). Then some simple graph on Fin (m + 2k m^2) has x adjacent to y exactly when, for some edge u < v of H and some p <= 2k, one of x, y is at position p and the other at position p + 1 of the path of (u, v).
title: For k >= 1, consecutive positions on the edge paths of a 2k-subdivision laid out on Fin (m + 2k m^2) form a simple graph
